task: Task 16 / S2 — ATT&CK-consistent attack path + time-to-progression
what_this_is: an ATT&CK-consistent progression hypothesis produced by composing the FROZEN V4 rollout with the EXISTING rule-based MITREMapper
what_this_is_not: not a guaranteed time until an attacker progresses
not a claim that V4 predicts ATT&CK labels
not a claim of attacker intent or causality
not a universally correct kill chain

substrate.mapper_threshold_note: the mapper is constructed with the FROZEN trajectory-MAX alert threshold (0.69). No per-horizon threshold was invented: the frozen per-horizon point thresholds cover k=1,2,3,5 only (k=4 has none by design), so interpolating one for k=4 would have meant inventing a threshold. A single frozen value is used at every horizon instead.
substrate.current_stage_gate_note: the CURRENT stage is gated on the NOWCAST probability (nowcast_probability_t0), because the current stage is a statement about now. The existing MITRE ATT&CK Timeline page gates on max-forecast instead; that difference is deliberate and is why most sequences report a current stage of 'No Alert' while the forecast is elevated.

reconstruction_procedure.row_0_current: NOT reconstructed — the observed 52-D vector screening_X[seq][-1] verbatim, exactly what src/mitre_mapper.py reads today
rows_1_to_5_rel_change: inverse-transform the base trajectory to RAW units with the frozen input_scaler base columns (z * scale + mean); the chain's k=0 element is the OBSERVED last window, so t+1's change is measured against reality
apply the frozen contract formula (x_k - x_{k-1}) / (|x_{k-1}| + 1e-8), clipped to [-10, 10]
forward-transform with the frozen input_scaler rel-change columns ((rel - mean) / scale)

decoder_space_identity.consequence: the V4 decoder's 26-D output is ALREADY in the mapper's base-feature z-units; no transform is applied to the base half

progression_graph.nature: project-specific ANALYTICAL ORDERING for forward visualisation. NOT a claim that intrusions follow this order, and NOT a universal kill chain.
progression_graph.node_source: exactly the tactics src/mitre_mapper.py can emit; no tactic was added

excluded_nodes.NONE / No Alert: no tactic semantics — cannot be an endpoint
excluded_nodes.UNKNOWN / Insufficient Evidence: no tactic semantics — cannot be an endpoint

edge_admission_test.i_ordering: B is ATT&CK-consistent as a stage following A, read through the SHIPPED RULE's meaning for each tactic
edge_admission_test.ii_distinguishability: the two rules key on materially different telemetry, so B-after-A is an observable signature change, not a relabelling

edges.justification: RECON_PORT_SCAN / RECON_HOST_DISCOVERY key on port breadth and port entropy; INITIAL_ACCESS_INFILTRATION keys on flow count with SYN+FIN completion. Enumeration preceding connection completion against a discovered service is the canonical ATT&CK ordering, and the two signatures differ (breadth vs. handshake completion).

LATERAL_MOVEMENT_SPREAD requires log_flow_count>0.5 AND log_unique_dst_ports>0.3 AND log_total_packets>0.3 — strictly more than the recon rules, which need no packet volume. Internal enumeration hardening into volumetric remote-service use is a real observable escalation, not a relabelling.

EXECUTION_PAYLOAD_DELIVERY keys on packet volume with PSH (data push), which is a different signature from the SYN/FIN handshake activity of the infiltration rule. Foothold then payload is the canonical ordering.

A channel established directly after access. C2_BEACONING / C2_ENCRYPTED_CHANNEL key on LOW packet-size variance and low protocol entropy — the opposite direction from the initial-access rule's volume/flag criteria, so the transition is clearly observable.
Payload delivery followed by channel establishment. Execution keys on high volume + PSH, C2 on low variance + download ratio.
Post-execution spread. Execution needs volume + PSH; lateral additionally needs port breadth, so lateral is a strict escalation.

IMPACT_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTION requires window_packet_rate>1.0 AND syn_rate>0.5 — by far the most extreme thresholds in the library. Execution escalating to a volumetric denial-of-service effect is ATT&CK-consistent and the signature is unambiguous.
Spread followed by channel consolidation; opposite telemetry directions (breadth/volume vs. uniform low-variance flows).
Collection across reached hosts leaving the network. Lateral keys on flow/port breadth, exfil on byte volume with LARGE mean packet length — volume-in-bytes rather than spread-in-flows.
The canonical ATT&CK ordering: an established channel then carries data out. C2 keys on small uniform packets, exfil on large packets and high byte rate, so the shift is directly observable.
Tasking over an established channel producing a destructive or volumetric effect.
Data theft followed by a destructive or disruptive effect.

time_to_progression.name: estimated model-based time-to-progression
time_to_progression.why_10s: each V4 rollout step advances the world model by exactly one 10-second feature window, the frozen WINDOW_SECONDS of the V4 ingestion contract
time_to_progression.k_definition: the FIRST predicted horizon k in 1..5 at which the candidate next stage is produced by the existing rule library and is reachable from the current stage by an admitted graph edge
time_to_progression.range: 10 s to 50 s, or undefined when no progression is identified
is_not: NOT a guaranteed time until an attacker progresses
NOT calibrated against observed progression times
NOT valid beyond 50 s — the V4 rollout is frozen at K=5
time_to_progression.suppressed_when: the Task-15 reliability status is UNRELIABLE; the panel then shows the warning instead of a bare precise-looking number

confidence_criteria.nature: deterministic three-level label. NOT a probability of stage correctness, NOT calibrated, NOT fitted.
inputs: persistence: length of the CONSECUTIVE run of future horizons, starting at the horizon where the candidate stage first appears, that carry the SAME tactic AND the SAME technique
rule_confidence: the existing MITREMapper confidence for the first horizon of that run (low|medium|high)
threat_stability: whether the frozen V4 threat probability stays at or above the FROZEN alert threshold across the whole run
confidence_criteria.HIGH: persistence >= 2 AND rule_confidence == 'high' AND threat_stability is True
confidence_criteria.MEDIUM: persistence >= 2 (any rule_confidence), OR (persistence == 1 AND rule_confidence == 'high' AND threat_stability is True)
confidence_criteria.LOW: everything else — a single weakly-supported horizon
confidence_criteria.no_tuning: the only numeric input is the frozen alert threshold read from screening_predictions.csv. No threshold was chosen, swept, or tuned on any label.

outputs.predictor_metadata.json: full machine-readable layer + rule library + graph description
outputs.retrospective_context.csv: 3 documented onset episodes + region x status cross-tab (DESCRIPTIVE ONLY)
outputs.example_cases.csv: real A / B / C examples, selected from model+rule output only

limitations: The progression graph is an analytical ordering for visualisation, not a model of attacker behaviour.
Stages inherit every limitation of the rule library, including single-check firing and hand-chosen z-score thresholds.
Future stages are read off a DECODED prediction; decoder reconstruction error at k=5 is inherited, not corrected.

The rel-change half of a future rule-space vector is reconstructed from the decoded base trajectory. It is faithful to the frozen formula but is a prediction of a derivative, so it is noisier than the base half. No shipped rule currently reads it.
Only 3 documented onset episodes exist in the replay substrate, so no general attack-stage accuracy can be claimed.
No stage label exists for this dataset, so no precision / recall / F1 over stages is computed or computable.
